title: Public art tiles stolen out of sidewalk in Dedham, town says
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: Four biodiversity-themed art tiles were stolen from Dedham's Sawmill Park Pollinator Pathway, set to open next week.
The Biodiversity Art Walk features 40 tiles funded by Massachusetts Community Biodiversity Grant, designed by local artists.
Dedham police will monitor the area; the Aug. 19 ribbon-cutting will proceed as planned, despite the theft.

title: The best waterfront hotel in America is in Massachusetts, according to USA Today readers
author: Kristi Palma
bullets: Chatham Bars Inn in Chatham, Massachusetts, ranked No. 1 in USA Today's 2026 Best Waterfront Hotels list.
The inn offers a quarter-mile private beach, ocean views, and five on-site dining options.
Madison Beach Hotel in Madison, Connecticut, ranked No. 4 on the same list.

title: Are millionaires really leaving Massachusetts? We don’t know yet.
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: IRS data is unavailable to confirm millionaire migration from Massachusetts after the 2023 millionaires tax implementation.
Massachusetts saw a 36% increase in millionaires between 2018 and 2022, but lower-tax states saw larger increases.
Massachusetts had a net domestic outflow of over 30,000 people in 2025, without income-specific migration data.

title: 7 things to do during a rainy day on the Cape
author: Kristi Palma
bullets: Chatham Shark Center offers interactive exhibits and shark story sessions for families on rainy days.
Visit Fins Up! Waterpark in Hyannis for slides and a lazy river; no resort stay needed.
Cape Cod museums include the JFK Museum in Hyannis and Wydah Pirate Museum in Yarmouth.

title: Visit to Boston made Boca Raton resident feel miserable about living in Boca Raton
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Ian Pinto's Boston trip left him dissatisfied with Boca Raton's limited walkability and high living costs.
Pinto enjoyed Boston's public transportation, affordable dining, and cultural openness during his four-day visit.
Pinto plans to travel more and hopes to move to Boston with his girlfriend in the future.

title: Motorcyclist killed in crash with pickup truck in Raynham
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: A 31-year-old motorcyclist, Jason Marshall of Taunton, was killed in a crash with a pickup truck in Raynham.
The crash occurred shortly before 8 p.m. at the intersection of Route 138 and Elm Street.
A 57-year-old driver of the Chevy Silverado involved in the crash remained on scene and spoke with police.

title: N.H. police seek to identify suspects who fatally shot dog in attempted armed robbery
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Hollis, NH police investigate an armed robbery where a dog was fatally shot on Laurel Hill Road.
A man and woman suspects demanded money from a victim, shooting his dog when he fled.
Police urge locals to review security footage from 2 a.m. to 4 a.m. Tuesday for suspect identification.

title: Former Red Sox infielder criticized front office: ‘Some people watch the game, some people go on the computer’
author: Hayden Bird
bullets: Vaughn Grissom criticizes Red Sox for over-reliance on analytics, affecting player development.
Grissom, now with the Angels, credits his improvement to organizational support rather than personal change.
Grissom maintains positive sentiment toward Red Sox players despite limited opportunities in Boston.

title: Authorities investigating 4 family members shot in N.H. as potential attempted murders and suicide
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: A 29-year-old man died by suicide after a shooting in a New Hampshire home involving four family members.
Amy Blake, Michael Marro, and Eric Blake Sr. were hospitalized with gunshot wounds; two are in critical condition.
Authorities are investigating the incident as potential attempted murders and a suicide, with no public threat identified.

title: Lindsay Clancy sobs in court as medical examiner testifies about children’s autopsies
author: Abby Patkin
bullets: Medical examiner Dr. Barbara Olson testified that the two oldest Clancy children died of asphyxia, with injuries consistent with ligature strangulation.
Lindsay Clancy broke down in court during testimony about her children's injuries, prompting an impromptu recess by Judge William Sullivan.
Dr. Renee Stonebridge testified that all three Clancy children showed signs of oxygen deprivation affecting their nervous systems and eyes.
